rows.evidence: Q1: Methodology/Case Study <U+2013> authors run a coupled MIKESHE/MIKE 11 model of the Mosuowan irrigation district using their own climate, soil, stream flow, irrigation and groundwater level data, calibrated and tested against 10 observation wells in 2006 (Fig. 3, Table 2). Q2: Introduction equates drip irrigation with water-saving irrigation; Results 'Effect of Irrigation Methods on Groundwater Recharge Intensity' and Fig. 4 <U+2013> simulated daily recharge was higher under flood irrigation (peaks 0.57 and 0.47 mm/d) than under water-saving irrigation (max 0.42, min 0.1 mm/d); authors conclude water-saving irrigation weakens recharge intensity, and Fig. 6 shows groundwater depth 0.37 m greater under water-saving irrigation; model outputs were compared with observed groundwater depths (E = 0.84, R = 0.92<U+2013>0.98). Q6: Case Study <U+2013> the result is reported for the whole Mosuowan irrigation district (about 45,100 ha), with spatial mapping of recharge-intensity change across the district (Fig. 5: 10.22% decreasing, 88.37% no change).
rows.notes: The comparison is between two different periods (flood irrigation 1991<U+2013>1992 vs water-saving irrigation 2006<U+2013>2007) and the authors note the irrigated area increased with no change in total supply, so the irrigation-method effect is confounded with land-use/area change. Drip is not named explicitly in the results; 'water-saving irrigation' is used, which the introduction equates with drip. Only one method (the model) underlies the result (Q3 no). Mechanism (reduced infiltration because the same water was spread over a larger area) is asserted as a reason, not reported as a separately measured or modelled intermediate variable (Q4 no). Single district (Q5 no). The elevation and land-use relations are gradients, not stated requirements (Q7 no). No limitations stated about the result; the generic non-uniqueness of groundwater models is discussed only in the introduction (Q8 no). Uncertainty reported is validation statistics (E, R, RMSE, 5<U+2013>95% regression bounds of simulated vs observed), not dispersion of the recharge difference (Q9 no).
